newsitem.title: USA: Dow index sets fifth straight record close.
newsitem.headline: Dow index sets fifth straight record close.

text.p: Blue-chip stocks ended in record territory Tuesday for the fifth straight session on expectations the Federal Reserve will stand pat on interest rates at Wednesday's policy-setting meeting of the Federal Open Market Committee.

The Dow Jones industrial average rose 10.44 points to 6,266.04, which beat Monday's record close of 6,255.60. It was the longest string of Dow records since the seven-session streak from Feb. 5 to 13.
"We don't expect any changes from the Fed," said Barbara Marcin, a vice president at Citibank Global Asset Management.
"The economic picture is almost perfectly mixed. We have middle-of-the-road politics, mediocre economic growth and low interest rates," she said. "We also don't expect surprises on inflation."
In the broader market, advancing issues led declines 1,325 to 1,102 on active volume of 471 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.

The bond market was also happy about the outlook for interest rates, as the benchmark 30-year Treasury bond rose 27/32, sending its yield down to an eight-month low of 6.44 percent from 6.51 percent on Friday. The bond market was closed Monday for the Veterans' Day holiday.

Bond traders also reflected optimism that bi-partisanship cooperation in Washington could lead to a resolution on a balanced budget and still-benign inflation numbers from the October Producer Price Index due on Wednesday and Consumer Price Index on Thursday.
Meanwhile, the Nasdaq Composite index closed 6.14 points lower at 1,256.53, hit by late selling in Intel Corp. and other technology stocks.
Intel, which hit a 52-week high at 125-1/8 early in the session on upbeat news about computer chip sales, lost 2-7/8 to 121 on profit-taking after recent strong gains.

"The market was in a mood to find an excuse for profit-taking," said Michael Metz, Oppenheimer and Co.'s chief investment strategist. "It's had an awfully nice run and traders are getting itchy here."

Analysts said technology stocks were also pressured by Microsoft Chairman Bill Gates' comments that an array of companies supporting the network computer movement posed the stiffest challenge the software giant has seen in years. Microsoft lost 1-7/8 to 141-3/4.

After Monday's market close, the Semiconductor Industry Association said the industry ratio of computer chip bookings to orders rose to 1.10 in October from 0.98 in September, stronger than analysts had expected.
Hildegard Zagorski, an analyst at Prudential Securities, said, "The book to bill was great but techs ran ahead of themselves and this afternoon they decided to take profits."

Among tech stocks, Micron fell 1-1/4 to 30-5/8, LSI Logic lost 1-1/8 to 31-1/8, Compaq shed 2-3/4 to 73-1/2, Dell Computer was off 1-3/4 to 88-5/8 and International Business Machines fell 1-3/8 to 133-1/8.
Among other individual issues, Wal-mart lost 1-1/4 to 25-1/4 after reporting third-quarter earnings that were less than expected.
Westinghouse rose 5/8 to 20-5/8. The company declined to comment on a Wall Street Journal report that it plans to spin off its industrial businesses into a separate company.
AT&T rose 1-1/4 to 38-3/8. The U.S. Supreme Court declined a request by federal regulators to reactivate rules meant to pry open local phone monopolies to competition.

Home Depot slumped 3-3/8 to 53-3/8 after reporting in-line quarterly results. Industry analysts said some investors had hoped for an even better quarter, while other investors worried about a possible peaking in the housing market.
Anchor Gaming slumped 8-7/8 to 30-1/8. The company announced that it was reconsidering plans to expand a Colorado casino, raising questions about Anchor's growth strategy.
The Standard & Poor's composite index of 500 stocks lost 2.31 points at 729.56. The American Stock Exchange index was up 1.92 to 581.55.
The NYSE Composite index of all listed common stocks fell 0.65 to 386.18. The average share was down 7 cents.
The Wilshire Associates Equity Index -- the market value of NYSE, American and Nasdaq issues -- was 7,067.640 down 15.004 or 0.21 percent.
